app.subtitulo: The journey of meteorites from their source to Earth
escena.descripcion: Interactive 3D visualization. When it has focus, the arrow keys rotate the camera, plus and minus zoom in or out, and zero resets the view. A text description of the view is in the control panel.
escala.visual.tierra: Visual scale: the fireball marker is enlarged (60 km radius). The atmospheric glow is a visual effect.
escala.visual.sistema-solar: Visual scale: Sun ×{sol}, inner planets ×{planetas}, Jupiter ×{jupiter}, and the meteoroid enlarged to a radius of ~900,000 km. Distances are real.
escala.real: True scale, with actual sizes and distances. The planets cannot be seen at this distance, so use the labels.
desc.tierra: Earth on {fecha} UTC. The orange line is the atmospheric entry trajectory of the Chelyabinsk fireball from an altitude of 100 km to peak brightness, at {alt} km over {lat}, {lon} (CNEOS data). The approach during the preceding hours comes from the orbit published by Popova and colleagues. The fall site of the meteorites is pending verification and is not shown.
desc.sistema-solar: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC, in the plane of the ecliptic. The orange cloud gathers {n} possible orbits of the Chelyabinsk meteoroid. They come from sampling the elements of the orbit published by Popova and colleagues within their 1σ uncertainty and keeping only those that pass by Earth at the moment of impact. The bright line is that orbit with all the digits they publish, and the trail is the path over the previous year, computed by N-body integration from the direction and speed at which it entered the atmosphere. Its perihelion lies near Venus and its aphelion near the asteroid belt.
error.datos: The visualization data could not be loaded.
narr.alejar: The camera pulls away from Earth.
narr.sistema: One year before reaching Earth, the meteoroid travels its orbit around the Sun. The cloud of points shows where it could be, given the measurement uncertainty.
narr.acercar: Days before arrival, the meteoroid and Earth approach the same point in their orbits.
narr.llegada: On the final day the meteoroid falls toward Earth, accelerated by its gravity.
narr.final: Peak brightness of the fireball over the Urals, {fecha} UTC. You can explore the scene or move the timeline.
narr.reducido: Reduced motion is on, so the full orbit is shown without animation. Use the timeline to step through it.
atajos.texto: Space plays or pauses. The left and right arrows move one day back or forward. I goes to peak brightness or to the reference point when the focus is not on a button or field. Escape skips the animation. With the focus on the scene (Tab key), the arrow keys rotate the camera, plus and minus zoom in or out, and zero resets the view. The same controls are on the Camera buttons. With a mouse or a finger, drag to rotate and scroll or pinch to zoom.
ficha.borrador: Draft pending human review. It is visible only in development and will not be published until it is approved.
ficha.fuentes: Sources for the data in this fact sheet
pieza.cuenta: {n} of {total} falls with a published orbit. Click a marker on the globe or choose from the list.
pieza.nombre-pendiente: Name as published by the source, pending verification in the Meteoritical Bulletin.
pieza.punto: Reference position of the luminous trajectory: {lat}, {lon} ({fuente}). This is not the fall site.
pieza.sin-punto: There is no verified position of the luminous trajectory, so it is not marked on the globe.
pieza.orbita: Orbit shown: a = {a}, e = {e}, i = {i} ({fuente}; 1σ uncertainty).
procedencia.escape: Escape route from the main belt
procedencia.escape-nota: Probability that the meteoroid reached the near-Earth region through each route, according to each source's dynamical model. The light band marks ±1σ.
procedencia.sin-asociacion: No association with a parent body.
escala.marcadores: The fall markers are position symbols, not objects to scale.
desc.tierra.pieza: Earth on {fecha} UTC. The highlighted marker is the reference position of the luminous trajectory of {nombre} ({lat}, {lon}), which is not the fall site. The other markers are the remaining falls with known orbits visible under the current filter ({n}).
desc.sistema-solar.pieza: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC. The blue cloud gathers {n} possible orbits of {nombre}, computed by sampling the radiant and geocentric velocity published by {fuente} within their 1σ uncertainty, so that all of them pass through Earth on the date of the fall. The faint clouds are the other visible falls. {regiones}
desc.sistema-solar.pieza.condicionada: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC. The blue cloud gathers {n} possible orbits of {nombre}, sampled within the 1σ uncertainty of the orbit published by {fuente} and keeping only those that pass by Earth at the moment of impact. The faint clouds are the other visible falls. {regiones}
desc.sistema-solar.pieza.jpl: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC. The blue cloud gathers {n} possible orbits of {nombre}, sampled within the 1σ uncertainty of the telescopic orbit from {fuente}, which is so small that the cloud almost shrinks to a line. The faint clouds are the other visible falls. {regiones}
desc.regiones: Approximate volumes are drawn for Hungaria, from ranges of osculating a and i ({f_hungaria}), and for Phocaea, from ranges in proper elements ({f_phocaea}), without eccentricity or the difference between proper and osculating elements. The dashed rings mark the nominal centers of the {resonancias} resonances with Jupiter. The ν6 resonance and the Jupiter-family comets have no geometry drawn.
escala.visual.tierra.pieza: Visual scale: the atmospheric glow is a visual effect.
cneos.actualizacion: Data from the CNEOS Fireball API (NASA/JPL). They are not continuously updated. Last data update {consultado} UTC, most recent event {ultimo}.
cneos.leyenda.no-verificable: Orbit cannot be verified (before {anio} and under {kt} kt)
cneos.leyenda.sin-trayectoria: No velocity vector or no altitude, position only
cneos.leyenda.tamano: Symbol size grows with impact energy (logarithmic scale). They are symbols, not objects to scale.
cneos.cuenta: {n} events with these filters, {g} of them placed on the globe ({total} records in all). Choose from the list or click a symbol.
cneos.recientes: All events, from most recent to oldest
cneos.evento.ubicacion: Peak brightness: {lat}, {lon}, at an altitude of {alt} km.
cneos.evento.energia: Radiated energy: {e} × 10¹⁰ J. Estimated impact energy: {kt} kt of TNT.
cneos.evento.comparacion.menor: About {factor} times less than Chelyabinsk ({ref} kt in the same record).
cneos.evento.comparacion.mayor: About {factor} times more than Chelyabinsk ({ref} kt in the same record).
cneos.evento.comparacion.igual: This is the Chelyabinsk fireball itself.
cneos.orbita.calculada: Computed here from the CNEOS velocity vector: {n} possible orbits. The median is shown and, in parentheses, the range that contains the central 68% of them (16th and 84th percentiles).
cneos.orbita.radiante: Computed geocentric radiant (nominal orbit): α {ra}°, δ {dec}°, geocentric velocity {vg} km/s.
cneos.orbita.hiperbolicas: {h} of the {n} possible orbits are hyperbolic (eccentricity greater than or equal to 1) and are drawn anyway. This may come from the error in the published velocity and is not taken to mean an object from outside the solar system.
cneos.orbita.sesgo: Warning: {d} of {p} simulations could not be completed, so the cloud may be biased toward the ones that did.
cneos.orbita.metodo: Method: the typical errors measured by Peña-Asensio et al. 2025 are applied to the geocentric radiant and to the entry velocity, and each variant is integrated backward with the Sun, the planets and the Moon. The range describes the variants of this model and is not a calibrated probability. For the study's reference events, the measured orbit fell within it about as often as expected.
cneos.orbita.error: The orbit could not be computed: {motivo}. This happens when the velocity relative to Earth is very low.
cneos.orbita.no-verificable: No orbit. For events before {anio} with less than {kt} kt, the typical error of the published velocity is {v} km/s and that of the radiant direction about {alfa}° (medians from Peña-Asensio et al. 2025), so the orbit cannot be verified in advance. Some of these events do have a good orbit.
cneos.orbita.sin-vector: No orbit or trajectory: CNEOS does not publish the velocity vector for this event.
cneos.orbita.sin-altura: No orbit or trajectory: CNEOS publishes the velocity vector but not the altitude for this event.
cneos.fuente: Source: CNEOS Fireball API (NASA/JPL). The orbits are computed here, not by CNEOS.
escala.marcadores.cneos: Fireball symbols show position and energy, not true size.
desc.tierra.cneos: Earth on {fecha} UTC. Each symbol is a fireball recorded by CNEOS ({n} with the current filters), and the highlighted one is selected.{tray} The data are not continuously updated (last update {consultado} UTC).
desc.tierra.cneos.tray: The bright line is its atmospheric entry trajectory to peak brightness, drawn from an altitude of {alto} km.
desc.sistema-solar.cneos: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC. The blue cloud gathers {n} possible orbits of the selected fireball, computed from variants of its velocity vector according to the typical errors measured on the geocentric radiant. The density of the cloud is not a calibrated probability.
desc.sistema-solar.cneos.sin: Inner solar system on {fecha} UTC. The selected fireball has no computed orbit. The reason is given in the panel.
escala.visual.sistema-solar.sin-meteoroi: Visual scale: Sun ×{sol}, inner planets ×{planetas} and Jupiter ×{jupiter}. Distances and orbits are real.
tiempo.sin-recorrido.cneos: CNEOS fireballs do not have an animated journey yet. The meteorites with known orbits do.
tiempo.sin-trayectoria: The animated journey for this meteorite is not available yet.
narr.final.pieza: Arrival of the {nombre} meteoroid in the atmosphere, {fecha} UTC. You can explore the scene or move the timeline.
desc.tierra.pieza.aprox: The orange line is its final approach, computed from the published radiant. It ends at the reference position at a conventional altitude of {alto} km, because the source does not publish the altitude.
desc.sistema-solar.pieza.tray: The bright trail is the meteoroid's path during the previous year, computed by N-body integration from the published radiant.
desc.tierra.pieza.aprox.jpl: The orange line is its final approach, computed from the state of the asteroid that JPL determined from telescopic observations before impact. At the reference moment it reaches an altitude of about {alto} km.
desc.sistema-solar.pieza.tray.jpl: The bright trail is the meteoroid's path during the previous year, computed by N-body integration from that JPL state. It matches JPL's telescopic orbit under the Drummond criterion (D_D = {dd}). It is not compared element by element in multiples of its uncertainty, because JPL's formal uncertainty is smaller than the precision of the ephemerides used here.
cneos.leyenda.orbita-fallida: Eligible for an orbit, but not computed (reason in the details)
cneos.cuenta.vacia: No event matches these filters ({total} records in all). Change the filters or reset them.
cneos.fuera-filtro: The selected event does not match the current filters. It is shown because it is still selected, not as a search result.
cneos.cuenta.fuera: The selected event is still on screen, but it does not match these filters.
cneos.buscar.ayuda: Use numbers and UTC, with a year, a year and month, or a full day (year-month-day or day/month/year).
cneos.leyenda.sin-ubicacion: No published location, so it appears only in the list and not on the globe
cneos.evento.sin-ubicacion: CNEOS does not publish the location of this event, so it does not appear on the globe.
cneos.orbita.sin-ubicacion: No orbit or trajectory. Without a published location they cannot be computed.
desc.tierra.cneos.sin-ubicacion: The selected event has no published location, so it does not appear on the globe.
cneos.orbita.pendiente: The orbit of this event has not been computed yet.
error.inicio: The basic visualization data could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
error.webgl: This browser or device cannot display the 3D scene (WebGL not available). The panels, data and sources are still available.
error.cneos: The CNEOS fireballs could not be loaded. The meteorites with known orbits are still available.
error.orbita: The orbit cloud for this fireball could not be loaded.
error.nubes: The orbit clouds for the meteorites could not be loaded.
error.trayectoria: The animated journey for this meteorite could not be loaded.
error.indice: Could not check which meteorites have an animated journey.
error.textura: The image of Earth could not be loaded, so the globe is shown without it.
error.contexto: The 3D scene stopped because the browser released the graphics card. It should recover on its own in a few seconds. If not, reload the page.
capas.seleccion: Possible orbits of the chosen meteorite, computed by sampling its radiant and velocity within the uncertainty published by its source. All of them pass through Earth on the date of the fall.
capas.otras: Possible orbits of the other falls with known orbits.
capas.estela: The meteoroid's trail over the previous year, computed with the Sun, the planets and the Moon. It is representative, and other paths are also consistent with the data.
capas.chelyabinsk: Possible orbits of Chelyabinsk, sampled within the uncertainty of the orbit by Popova and colleagues (the one cited in its fact sheet). Only those passing by Earth are kept. The bright line is that orbit.
capas.hungaria: Hungaria region, approximate volume according to Warner and colleagues.
capas.phocaea: Phocaea region, approximate volume according to Novaković and colleagues.
capas.resonancias: Resonances with Jupiter, drawn at their nominal center and without the width of the zone.
capas.cneos: Orbits computed from variants of the CNEOS vector, according to the typical errors that Peña-Asensio and colleagues measured on the geocentric radiant.
capas.densidad: Where a cloud looks denser there are more variants of the model, which is not a calibrated probability of where the object was.
luz.aviso.presentacion: Always daytime: the visible side of the globe is lit even if it was night there at that moment. The light does not come from the Sun's real position. Turn this off to see the light of that moment.
luz.aviso.real: Real light: the globe is lit by the Sun at that moment, and the night side looks dark.
desc.luz.presentacion: The globe is always shown in daylight, with presentation lighting that does not match the Sun's real position.
desc.luz.real: The globe is lit by the Sun at that moment.
economico.aviso: Low-power mode: lower resolution and no glow effect, to use less battery. The data are the same.
economico.aviso.auto: Low-power mode turned on automatically because the scene was running slowly on this device. It uses a lower resolution and no glow effect, but the data are the same.
